reply_text:
**Don't merge yet.** There's one blocking bug and one risky behavior change. The 5 tests pass, but they miss both problems. I didn't change anything in the repo.

**1. Blocking: one flag's rules can turn on other flags** (`flags/registry.py`)
`add_rule(flag_name, rule, rules=[])` uses a list as a default argument. Python creates that list once and reuses it on every call. So every flag built without an explicit `rules` argument ends up sharing one rule list. I confirmed it: after `add_rule('a', {'plan':'pro'})` and `add_rule('b', {'region':'eu'})`, flag **b** is on for `{'plan':'pro'}`, and both flags hold the same list. That breaks the README's promise that "Flags are independent" and "A fresh flag starts with no rules." In rollout config, that means features turn on for the wrong users. The tests don't catch it because every call passes `[]` explicitly.
Fix: default to `rules=None`, then use `rules = list(rules or []) + [rule]`. Copying the list also stops chained flags from changing each other. Add a test that calls `add_rule` twice without `rules` and checks the flags stay separate.

**2. Risky: the new matching is looser than the docs say** (`flags/match.py`)
Matching now converts both sides to lowercase strings (`str(...).lower()`), which goes beyond the documented "case-insensitive, str/int":
• A missing field becomes the text `"none"`, so `{'x': 'None'}` matches a context that has no `x` at all. I confirmed this.
• `True` matches `"TRUE"`/`"true"`, and `1.0` won't match `1`.
• This changes how every existing rule is evaluated. Check whether any rule in production relied on exact matching.
Suggest returning False when the key is missing, and limiting the normalization to what the docs describe.

**3. Minor**
• `in_rollout` has no test for anything between 0 and 100, and nothing checks that `percent` is in range. The same user lands in the same bucket for every flag. Consider adding the flag name to the hash so a 10% rollout doesn't always hit the same 10% of users.
• The README says to chain rules by passing `flag.rules` back in. Until #1 is fixed, that modifies the earlier flag too.
• The changelog is missing the matching change from #2, and it changes behavior.

Fix #1 and it's mergeable. I'd also settle #2 before release.
